title: Data Center Growth Brings New Demands for Refrigerant Leak Detection
summary: Data centers depend on nonstop cooling, making early refrigerant leak detection essential for protecting efficiency, uptime, and compliance. As facilities scale and adopt newer refrigerants, continuous monitoring helps prevent performance loss and unnecessary energy use. MSA Safety provides advanced solutions that support reliable, compliant cooling operations.
body_text: Reading Time: 3 minutes Cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and digital services are driving demand for new data centers worldwide. These facilities are becoming critical infrastructure, supporting everything from business operations to online communications and emerging technologies. Behind every data center is a cooling system working continuously to maintain temperatures that support reliable equipment performance. But even the smallest refrigerant leak can affect cooling efficiency, increase operating costs, raise compliance concerns, and, in some cases, contribute to unplanned downtime. Refrigerant leak detection should be a top priority in the design, maintenance, and operation of data center cooling systems. Cooling Systems Are a Critical Component of Data Center Operations Modern data centers generate significant amounts of heat. To maintain safe operating temperatures, facilities rely on complex cooling systems to prevent equipment and spaces from overheating. These cooling systems operate continuously, and refrigerant leaks can pose challenges beyond routine maintenance. Undetected leaks may substantially increase costs through issues like: Reduced cooling efficiency Increased energy consumption Higher refrigerant replacement costs Potential regulatory compliance issues Increased risk of equipment failure and downtime Given the cost of data center outages and the growing pressure to improve energy efficiency, facility operators are placing greater emphasis on continuous refrigerant monitoring and early leak detection. Why Early Leak Detection Matters Detecting refrigerant leaks early allows operators to address issues before they affect system performance. Small leaks can gradually reduce cooling capacity while increasing energy demand. Over time, this can place additional strain on equipment and shorten component life. Early detection helps maintenance teams identify problems sooner, reducing the likelihood of larger, more expensive repairs and helping facilities maintain efficient operations. Leak detection also supports compliance with refrigeration safety standards and emissions regulations that apply to some data centers’ cooling systems. As cooling technologies evolve and facilities adopt newer refrigerants, including A2L refrigerant gases, monitoring solutions should be capable of supporting a wide range of applications and refrigerant types. MSA Safety’s portfolio of safety and efficiency equipment includes an extensive range of solutions for multiple aspects of data centers, including trusted refrigerant leak detectors capable of detecting legacy and modern refrigerant gases. Improving Data Center Resilience with Intelligent Safety Solutions To learn more about MSA Safety’s suite of data center safety and efficiency solutions, check out this detailed white paper. GET THE WHITEPAPER Refrigerant Monitoring Solutions for Data Centers MSA Safety offers refrigerant monitoring technologies that can help data center operators detect leaks early, support compliance efforts, and maintain cooling system performance. Bacharach® Multi-Zone Gas Monitor Data centers often contain multiple cooling assets spread throughout large facilities. The Bacharach Multi-Zone Gas Monitor helps centralize refrigerant monitoring across multiple locations while offering a minimum detection level of just 1 ppm for halogenated gases. The Multi-Zone Gas Monitor can identify leaks early, helping reduce refrigerant loss, support energy efficiency efforts, and assist facilities in meeting requirements associated with refrigeration safety standards and emissions regulations, including ASHRAE 15, EN 378, CSA-B52, F-Gas, and CARB RMP. Bacharach® MGS-550 Dual Gas Detector Facilities often require monitoring for multiple gas types. The Bacharach MGS-550 Dual Gas Detector is designed to detect refrigerants, including modern A2L refrigerants, as well as toxic and combustible gases. The MGS-550 can utilize many combinations of sensor technologies, including electrochemical, semiconductor (MOS), catalytic bead, and/or infrared, in a single platform for exceptional detection capabilities. This allows operators to address a range of monitoring requirements while helping meet standards such as ASHRAE 15 and EN 378. This flexibility can be particularly valuable in data center environments where cooling technologies and facility requirements continue to evolve. Chillgard® 5000 Refrigerant Leak Monitor For applications where early leak detection is vital, the Chillgard 5000 Refrigerant Leak Monitor provides detection capabilities down to 1 ppm. Using patented photoacoustic infrared (PAIR) technology, the Chillgard 5000 is designed to detect refrigerant leaks before they become larger issues. The monitor supports the detection of traditional refrigerants as well as modern A2L refrigerants, making it suitable for a variety of mechanical room and cooling system applications found in today’s data centers. Supporting Data Center Reliability Through Monitoring As data centers continue to expand, maintaining reliable cooling performance is critical to responsible operation. Refrigerant monitoring allows operators to identify leaks sooner, helping maintain cooling efficiency, supporting compliance programs, and reducing unnecessary refrigerant loss. While refrigerant leak detection is an important part of data center operations, it is only one component of a broader safety and monitoring strategy. From personal protective equipment used during construction and maintenance activities to fixed gas and flame detection systems and integrated monitoring technologies, MSA Safety provides solutions that support data centers from groundbreaking to operations. For a deeper look at the safety, monitoring, and operational challenges facing today’s data centers, download our Data Center Solutions White Paper. You can also visit our Data Center Solutions page to learn more about technologies that support data center construction, operation, and maintenance. title: Utang Negara Indonesia, Jumlah, dan Dampaknya bagi Ekonomi
summary: Berapa utang negara Indonesia? Pelajari sumber utang, rasio terhadap GDP, perbandingan dengan negara ASEAN, dan dampaknya terhadap ekonomi masyarakat.
body_text: Utang negara Indonesia adalah salah satu topik ekonomi yang paling banyak dibicarakan masyarakat. Angkanya besar, trennya terus bergerak, dan dampaknya terasa hingga ke kehidupan sehari-hari. Namun, tidak sedikit orang yang salah paham tentang apa sebenarnya utang negara itu, bagaimana cara kerjanya, dan apakah kondisi saat ini perlu dikhawatirkan. Artikel ini menyajikan penjelasan objektif tentang kondisi utang negara Indonesia — berapa jumlahnya, dari mana sumbernya, bagaimana perbandingannya dengan negara-negara ASEAN, serta apa dampaknya terhadap ekonomi dan keuangan masyarakat. Berapa Total Utang Negara Indonesia Saat Ini? Per akhir 2024, total utang pemerintah pusat Indonesia mencapai sekitar Rp8.680 triliun, atau setara dengan lebih dari 39% terhadap Produk Domestik Bruto (PDB). Angka ini bersumber dari laporan resmi Kementerian Keuangan Republik Indonesia yang dipublikasikan secara berkala melalui kemenkeu.go.id . Penting untuk dipahami bahwa jumlah nominal utang yang besar tidak serta-merta berarti kondisinya berbahaya. Yang lebih relevan untuk dinilai adalah rasio utang terhadap PDB, kualitas pengelolaan utang, serta kemampuan negara dalam membayar kewajiban. Indonesia memiliki batas hukum rasio utang pemerintah terhadap PDB sebesar 60%, sebagaimana diatur dalam Undang-Undang Nomor 17 Tahun 2003 tentang Keuangan Negara. Dengan rasio sekitar 38–40%, Indonesia masih berada jauh di bawah batas tersebut. Apa Perbedaan Utang Pemerintah dan Utang Luar Negeri Swasta? Banyak orang menyamakan “utang negara” dengan “utang luar negeri Indonesia” secara keseluruhan. Padahal, keduanya berbeda secara signifikan dan perlu dipahami secara terpisah. Utang Pemerintah Utang pemerintah adalah kewajiban finansial yang ditanggung oleh pemerintah pusat dalam rangka membiayai APBN. Utang ini digunakan untuk mendanai infrastruktur, layanan publik, subsidi, dan program pembangunan nasional. Pemerintah bertanggung jawab langsung atas pembayaran pokok dan bunganya. Utang Luar Negeri Swasta Utang luar negeri swasta adalah pinjaman yang dilakukan oleh perusahaan atau lembaga keuangan swasta kepada kreditur asing. Utang ini tidak menjadi beban APBN secara langsung, dan tanggung jawab pembayarannya berada pada entitas swasta yang bersangkutan. Utang Luar Negeri Indonesia Secara Keseluruhan Bank Indonesia mencatat bahwa total utang luar negeri Indonesia — yang mencakup utang pemerintah maupun swasta — secara historis berada pada kisaran USD 400 miliar lebih. Data terkini dapat diakses melalui situs resmi Bank Indonesia . Memahami perbedaan dua komponen ini penting agar masyarakat tidak keliru menginterpretasikan berita ekonomi. Sumber-Sumber Utang Negara Indonesia Pemerintah Indonesia memperoleh pinjaman dari dua sumber utama: penerbitan surat utang dan pinjaman langsung. Surat Berharga Negara (SBN) Sebagian besar utang pemerintah bersumber dari penerbitan Surat Berharga Negara (SBN), yang mencakup Surat Utang Negara (SUN) dan Surat Berharga Syariah Negara (SBSN) atau sukuk negara. SBN diterbitkan di pasar domestik maupun internasional dan dapat dibeli oleh investor individu maupun institusi. Beberapa instrumen SBN yang tersedia untuk masyarakat umum antara lain Obligasi Ritel Indonesia (ORI), Sukuk Ritel (SR), Savings Bond Ritel (SBR), dan Sukuk Tabungan (ST). Instrumen-instrumen ini memungkinkan masyarakat ikut berpartisipasi dalam pembiayaan negara sekaligus memperoleh imbal hasil. Pinjaman Bilateral dan Multilateral Pemerintah juga menerima pinjaman langsung dari negara-negara mitra (bilateral) seperti Jepang, Prancis, Jerman, dan Korea Selatan, serta dari lembaga keuangan internasional (multilateral) seperti Bank Dunia, Asian Development Bank (ADB), dan Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). Pinjaman jenis ini umumnya digunakan untuk proyek-proyek spesifik seperti pembangunan infrastruktur transportasi, sanitasi, pendidikan, dan ketahanan pangan. Suku bunganya biasanya lebih rendah dibanding obligasi komersial karena bersifat konsesional. Rasio Utang terhadap GDP: Apakah Aman? Rasio utang terhadap PDB adalah indikator utama untuk menilai kesehatan fiskal suatu negara. Indikator ini mengukur seberapa besar utang pemerintah dibandingkan dengan total output ekonomi negara dalam satu tahun. Rasio utang Indonesia terhadap PDB berada di kisaran 38–40%, jauh di bawah ambang batas 60% yang ditetapkan undang-undang. Dana Moneter Internasional (IMF) umumnya menganggap rasio di bawah 60% sebagai zona yang relatif aman bagi negara berkembang. Namun, rasio saja tidak cukup untuk menilai risiko. Faktor lain yang penting diperhatikan meliputi: Komposisi mata uang utang (rupiah vs valuta asing) Profil jatuh tempo (jangka pendek vs jangka panjang) Tingkat suku bunga yang berlaku Kapasitas penerimaan pajak negara Stabilitas nilai tukar rupiah Kementerian Keuangan secara konsisten mempublikasikan laporan pengelolaan utang yang dapat diakses publik sebagai bentuk transparansi fiskal. Perbandingan Utang Indonesia vs Negara ASEAN Lainnya Menempatkan utang Indonesia dalam konteks regional membantu memberikan perspektif yang lebih objektif. Berikut adalah perbandingan estimasi rasio utang pemerintah terhadap PDB di negara-negara ASEAN berdasarkan data IMF dan bank sentral masing-masing negara: Negara Rasio Utang/PDB (estimasi 2023–2024) Singapura ~170% (utang domestik untuk pengembangan pasar modal) Malaysia ~65% Thailand ~62% Filipina ~60% Vietnam ~37% Indonesia ~38–40% Kamboja ~35% Catatan: Rasio utang Singapura yang tinggi bersifat unik karena sebagian besar merupakan utang domestik yang diterbitkan untuk keperluan pengembangan pasar keuangan, bukan untuk membiayai defisit anggaran. Jika dibandingkan secara apple-to-apple, posisi Indonesia tergolong moderat di antara negara-negara ASEAN. Malaysia dan Thailand memiliki rasio yang lebih tinggi dari Indonesia, namun keduanya juga memiliki kapasitas penerimaan pajak dan basis ekonomi yang berbeda. Perbandingan ini menunjukkan bahwa Indonesia bukan yang paling tinggi berutang di kawasan. Tren Utang Negara Indonesia dalam 10 Tahun Terakhir Memahami tren utang pemerintah dari waktu ke waktu jauh lebih bermakna daripada sekadar melihat angka terkini. Berikut adalah gambaran tren utang pemerintah Indonesia dalam satu dekade terakhir berdasarkan data Kementerian Keuangan: Tahun Total Utang Pemerintah (estimasi) Rasio terhadap PDB 2015 Rp3.165 triliun ~27% 2016 Rp3.466 triliun ~28% 2017 Rp3.938 triliun ~29% 2018 Rp4.418 triliun ~30% 2019 Rp4.779 triliun ~30% 2020 Rp6.074 triliun ~39% 2021 Rp6.908 triliun ~41% 2022 Rp7.733 triliun ~39% 2023 Rp8.144 triliun ~38% 2024 Rp8.680 triliun ~39% Lonjakan paling signifikan terjadi pada 2020, ketika pemerintah memperlebar defisit APBN hingga melampaui 3% PDB sebagai respons terhadap pandemi COVID-19. Kebijakan ini diambil berdasarkan Perppu Nomor 1 Tahun 2020 yang kemudian menjadi UU Nomor 2 Tahun 2020, yang memberikan fleksibilitas fiskal luar biasa selama masa darurat. Sejak 2022, rasio utang terhadap PDB cenderung stabil bahkan sedikit menurun, menandakan upaya konsolidasi fiskal yang dilakukan pemerintah pascapandemi. Pemerintah berkomitmen untuk kembali ke defisit di bawah 3% PDB, yang secara bertahap menekan laju pertumbuhan utang baru. Untuk Apa Utang Negara Digunakan? Utang negara bukan sekadar angka di neraca keuangan pemerintah. Dana yang diperoleh digunakan untuk membiayai berbagai program yang berdampak langsung pada kehidupan masyarakat. Pembiayaan Infrastruktur Sebagian besar utang pemerintah dalam satu dekade terakhir digunakan untuk membangun infrastruktur: jalan tol, pelabuhan, bandara, pembangkit listrik, dan jaringan kereta api. Infrastruktur ini diharapkan meningkatkan konektivitas dan daya saing ekonomi nasional dalam jangka panjang. Pembayaran Subsidi dan Perlindungan Sosial Dana utang juga digunakan untuk membiayai subsidi energi, subsidi pangan, dan berbagai program perlindungan sosial seperti Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH), Kartu Sembako, dan Kartu Indonesia Pintar (KIP). Program-program ini menjangkau jutaan keluarga berpenghasilan rendah. Pembiayaan Defisit APBN Setiap tahun, pengeluaran pemerintah melebihi penerimaan pajak dan non-pajak. Selisih inilah yang disebut defisit anggaran, dan utang adalah instrumen utama untuk menutupnya. Defisit bukan sesuatu yang otomatis buruk — hampir semua negara di dunia menjalankan defisit anggaran pada tingkat tertentu. Dampak Utang Negara terhadap Ekonomi Masyarakat Utang negara memiliki dampak yang luas dan berlapis terhadap kondisi ekonomi masyarakat, mulai dari inflasi hingga nilai tukar rupiah. Dampak terhadap Inflasi Ketika pemerintah meningkatkan belanja melalui utang tanpa diimbangi produktivitas ekonomi yang setara, tekanan inflasi dapat meningkat. Dana yang beredar lebih banyak dapat mendorong permintaan barang dan jasa, sehingga harga-harga cenderung naik. Namun, dampak ini sangat bergantung pada bagaimana dana utang digunakan. Jika utang diinvestasikan pada proyek-proyek produktif yang meningkatkan kapasitas produksi, efek inflasinya cenderung minimal karena pertumbuhan sisi penawaran mengimbangi sisi permintaan. Dampak terhadap Nilai Tukar Rupiah Utang pemerintah dalam bentuk valuta asing menciptakan kewajiban pembayaran yang harus dilakukan dalam mata uang asing — terutama dolar AS. Ketika jumlah utang valas besar dan jatuh tempo bersamaan, permintaan terhadap dolar meningkat, yang dapat menekan nilai rupiah. Pelemahan rupiah, pada gilirannya, meningkatkan beban pembayaran utang valas dalam hitungan rupiah, dan berpotensi mendorong inflasi impor — yaitu kenaikan harga barang yang komponen impornya signifikan. Dampak terhadap Suku Bunga Pemerintah yang menerbitkan SBN dalam jumlah besar di pasar domestik dapat bersaing dengan sektor swasta dalam memperebutkan dana masyarakat. Kondisi ini berpotensi mendorong suku bunga naik — yang berarti kredit menjadi lebih mahal bagi pelaku usaha dan individu. Dampak terhadap Anggaran Publik Semakin besar utang, semakin besar pula porsi APBN yang harus dialokasikan untuk pembayaran bunga dan pokok utang. Ini berarti ruang fiskal untuk membiayai layanan publik, pendidikan, kesehatan, dan infrastruktur baru menjadi lebih sempit dari waktu ke waktu. Apakah Utang Indonesia Aman? Perspektif Ekonom Para ekonom umumnya menilai kondisi utang Indonesia saat ini masih berada dalam batas yang terkelola, dengan beberapa catatan penting. Dari sisi positif, rasio utang terhadap PDB Indonesia masih di bawah ambang batas 60% yang ditetapkan undang-undang, dan jauh di bawah rata-rata negara maju yang bisa mencapai 100% lebih. Komposisi utang dalam negeri yang semakin besar juga dianggap lebih aman karena mengurangi eksposur terhadap risiko nilai tukar. Namun, sejumlah risiko tetap perlu diwaspadai. Pertama, beban bunga utang yang terus meningkat menggerus ruang fiskal pemerintah. Kedua, kepemilikan SBN oleh investor asing yang cukup besar menjadikan pasar obligasi Indonesia rentan terhadap gejolak modal keluar (capital outflow) ketika sentimen global memburuk. Ketiga, nilai tukar rupiah yang melemah secara langsung meningkatkan beban utang valas dalam denominasi rupiah. Lembaga pemeringkat seperti Moody’s, S&P, dan Fitch secara konsisten memberikan peringkat investment grade kepada Indonesia, yang mencerminkan kepercayaan pasar internasional terhadap kemampuan Indonesia dalam mengelola kewajiban keuangannya. Data dan laporan terkini dari Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) juga dapat menjadi referensi untuk memantau kondisi stabilitas keuangan secara berkala. Apa yang Bisa Dilakukan Masyarakat di Tengah Dinamika Ekonomi Makro? Kondisi utang negara adalah bagian dari dinamika ekonomi makro yang tidak bisa dikendalikan langsung oleh individu. Namun, setiap orang memiliki kendali penuh atas kondisi keuangan pribadinya sendiri. Di tengah ketidakpastian ekonomi — baik karena tekanan inflasi, pergerakan nilai tukar, maupun kebijakan suku bunga — langkah paling bijak adalah memperkuat fondasi keuangan pribadi. Ini mencakup membangun dana darurat, mendiversifikasi simpanan, dan memilih instrumen keuangan yang memberikan imbal hasil nyata di atas inflasi. Fazza hadir sebagai platform keuangan digital yang membantu masyarakat mengelola dan mengembangkan keuangan pribadi dengan lebih cerdas. Dengan produk tabungan berbunga tinggi dan simpanan berjangka yang transparan, Fazza memudahkan siapa saja untuk mulai mengamankan keuangan pribadi — tanpa kerumitan perbankan konvensional. Unduh aplikasi Fazza sekarang dan mulai kelola keuanganmu dengan lebih bijak: Download Fazza di Google Play Store Download Fazza di App Store FAQ: Utang Negara Indonesia Apakah utang negara berarti setiap warga negara menanggung utang tersebut? Tidak secara langsung. Utang pemerintah dibayar menggunakan penerimaan negara, seperti pajak dan sumber pendapatan lainnya. Artinya, masyarakat berkontribusi melalui penerimaan negara, tetapi utang tersebut bukan merupakan kewajiban pribadi yang harus dibayar oleh setiap warga negara secara langsung. Apa bedanya utang pemerintah dengan utang luar negeri Indonesia? Utang pemerintah adalah pinjaman yang menjadi kewajiban pemerintah pusat. Sementara itu, utang luar negeri Indonesia mencakup seluruh pinjaman luar negeri yang dimiliki oleh pemerintah, Bank Indonesia, dan sektor swasta. Dengan demikian, nilai utang luar negeri Indonesia secara keseluruhan biasanya lebih besar dibandingkan utang pemerintah saja. Apakah utang negara Indonesia bisa menyebabkan krisis seperti tahun 1998? Kondisi saat ini berbeda dengan krisis ekonomi tahun 1998. Saat itu, krisis dipicu oleh berbagai faktor, termasuk tingginya utang swasta dalam valuta asing, lemahnya sistem perbankan, dan gejolak nilai tukar. Meski demikian, pemerintah tetap perlu mengelola utang secara hati-hati karena faktor ekonomi global, perubahan suku bunga, dan fluktuasi nilai tukar tetap dapat memengaruhi kondisi perekonomian. Bagaimana cara masyarakat memantau perkembangan utang negara? Masyarakat dapat memantau perkembangan utang negara melalui laporan resmi yang diterbitkan oleh Kementerian Keuangan, seperti laporan APBN bulanan, serta data yang dipublikasikan oleh Bank Indonesia mengenai utang luar negeri. Seluruh informasi tersebut tersedia secara terbuka melalui kanal resmi pemerintah. Apakah utang negara dalam rupiah lebih aman daripada utang dalam dolar? Secara umum, utang dalam rupiah memiliki risiko nilai tukar yang lebih rendah karena pembayarannya menggunakan mata uang yang sama dengan sebagian besar penerimaan negara. Sebaliknya, utang dalam mata uang asing memiliki risiko tambahan karena beban pembayaran dapat meningkat apabila nilai tukar rupiah melemah terhadap mata uang tersebut. Mengapa pemerintah tidak mengurangi utang dengan mencetak uang lebih banyak? Mencetak uang secara berlebihan untuk membayar utang dapat memicu inflasi yang tinggi dan mengganggu stabilitas ekonomi. Oleh karena itu, kebijakan pencetakan uang dilakukan secara hati-hati oleh bank sentral dengan mempertimbangkan kondisi ekonomi dan tujuan menjaga stabilitas nilai rupiah. Apa dampak utang negara terhadap generasi muda Indonesia? Utang negara yang digunakan saat ini akan menjadi bagian dari tanggung jawab fiskal di masa depan. Namun, apabila utang tersebut dimanfaatkan untuk investasi produktif seperti pembangunan infrastruktur, pendidikan, dan layanan kesehatan, manfaatnya juga dapat dirasakan oleh generasi muda melalui peningkatan kualitas ekonomi dan pelayanan publik.

title: Procurement on the pitch: moving from defense to offense with AI
summary: AI is automating procurement's manual work. See how CPOs can move their teams from defense to offense, and what the data says about redeploying talent.
body_text: Every Chief Procurement Officer is asking some version of the same question right now, which is “what does my team look like a year from now?” Intake and orchestration AI is automating the work that used to fill the day, from the data entry and validation to the handoffs between disconnected point solutions. Work that once ate real team bandwidth now runs on its own, and every procurement leader has a decision to make. And I think Spain’s World Cup win last Sunday can actually teach quite a lot about how to build a winning team. Key takeaways AI is automating procurement's manual work, and that forces a choice between shrinking the team and moving it up the pitch to strategic work. The leaders are choosing to redeploy. The builders prove it with behavior. 54% have already cut or consolidated roles while 49% still expect their teams to grow, against just 8% of bystanders who have cut. The cut and the hire are the same move. The work that's growing is strategic oversight. Evaluating and fact-checking AI output is the single most in-demand skill at 49%, ahead of managing AI compliance and designing automated workflows. For the full builders-vs-bystanders data on ROI, hiring, and team design, read the State of AI in Spend report . Procurement's AI fork in the road: cut headcount or redeploy talent Procurement has long been asked to do more on the same budget. As AI and orchestration Superagents clear out the manual work, that pressure sharpens, and leaders are feeling it. In our State of AI in Spend report, a survey of 1,050 global procurement, finance, IT, and operations leaders, the share of teams expecting a smaller function in five years doubled in twelve months, from 17% to 34%, while growth optimism fell from 38% to 28%. Nearly half of organizations have cut or plan to cut roles because AI can now do the work (29% already have, another 19% plan to). That transformation pressure brings us to a fork in the road: Option A: Shrink the org. Cut roles where AI now does the work, capture the efficiency, and hand the headcount savings back to the business. Option B: Redeploy. Treat this as a rare inflection point and move that talent toward the strategic, value-generating work procurement has always been capable of and rarely had the capacity to pursue. For forward-thinking leaders, the answer is usually with Option B or a blend of both, and the data backs the instinct. The report splits respondents into ‘Builders,’ the organizations showing clear, measurable ROI from AI, and ‘Bystanders,’ the ones still stuck in pilots. Builders are doing both things at once: while most have eliminated or consolidated roles, they’re at the same time growing their team. The Builders are cutting and hiring the same move. They're recomposing the team around higher-value work and hiring into the space that opens up. To get there, you need to rethink what procurement is for. The answer seems to be right there on the soccer field. A World Cup framework for procurement's role in the AI era Last Sunday's FIFA World Cup final made this framework come to life on the field. Spain spent 120 minutes pressing forward, took 20 shots, and finally broke through when substitute Ferran Torres struck in extra time for a 1-0 win. Argentina spent the match doing the opposite: sitting deep, absorbing pressure, and betting they could survive to penalties. They didn't manage a shot until extra time. The side built to attack won; the side built only to defend went home. Let’s take a step back. Imagine 22 players spread across the field, each in a distinct position, each with a distinct role. The team's success depends on more than individual talent. It depends on how those roles are structured, how cleanly players move between phases of play, and whether the side is built to attack or only to defend. For years, the limits of procurement technology forced the function into a defensive formation. Think of the backfield: defenders and goalkeepers whose whole job is preventing bad outcomes. In procurement terms, that has meant: Goalkeeping against rogue requisitions and unauthorized spend Defending against late stakeholder engagement and compliance failures Enforcing process gates so every required step gets completed before the ball moves forward This is no knock on the professionals playing those roles; they're doing exactly what a fragmented, manual, reactive system relegates them to. They spend their days chasing approvals, correcting data, and policing process adherence. Their tools demand it, even though it's nowhere near the highest use of their skills. The result is a function held back from the value it could deliver, the value finance leaders and business stakeholders have always expected from it. How orchestration AI shifts procurement to an offensive formation AI procurement orchestration changes how the game gets played. When it handles the defensive work, validating data, routing workflows, holding the compliance line, connecting systems that don't talk to each other, procurement professionals are free to move up the pitch. And the freed-up time is real: 89% of leaders in our report say AI is a net productivity gain even after they account for correcting its mistakes, with 21% calling it a significant one. So what does an offensive procurement formation look like? Midfield: the strategic connector. Midfielders are the engine of the team, linking defense to attack, distributing the ball, creating chances. In procurement, that's the category manager who engages stakeholders before a need becomes a crisis, brings market intelligence and supplier insight to the table early, and shapes demand instead of simply fulfilling it. Striker: the value creator. Strikers drive toward goal. In procurement, that's the strategic advisor who builds category strategies aligned to enterprise objectives and works suppliers proactively to spark innovation, lift performance, and tie supplier capability to the company's mission. This is the work procurement professionals have always aspired to do. It's also the work CFOs, CPOs, and business leaders have always expected from procurement and rarely seen delivered consistently, because the team was too busy defending. Rebuilding the squad: AI's impact on procurement talent and org design The move from defensive to offensive procurement is a talent and organizational design story as much as a technology one. You can already see it in what teams are staffing for. The single most in-demand capability in our report is evaluating and fact-checking AI output (49%), ahead of managing AI compliance and risk and designing automated workflows. Someone still has to check the AI, and that someone is increasingly a strategic hire. The recomposition shows up most clearly at the entry level. Among bystanders, 69% say junior roles are roughly the same as before; among builders, only 21% do. The leaders are actively reshaping early-career work. CPOs who seize this inflection point will: Redefine roles. Move people off process enforcement and toward stakeholder advisory, supplier development, and category strategy. Invest in capability building. Equip teams with the commercial, analytical, and relationship skills a strategic advisor needs. Retire the low-value work. Help team members see AI-driven automation as a release from tasks they were always overqualified to perform. Become an employer of choice. Give every team member tools and processes that let them operate at the top of their capability, and attract the talent that will define procurement's next chapter. There's a principle underneath all of this is that tools should work for people. For too long, procurement professionals have worked for their tools, compensating for system shortcomings through manual effort, workarounds, and sheer persistence. The next generation of procurement technology flips that relationship. The CPO playbook for the AI transition This is a rare window. The CPOs who resist the short-term temptation to simply cut headcount, and instead invest in repositioning their organizations, will build procurement functions that deliver value worth multiples of their cost. Some leaders are already wiring this into how they hire. In our report, 7% of organizations now require a manager to justify why AI can't do a job before they're allowed to bring on a human. Whatever you make of the policy, the front-runners are already treating every hire as a capacity decision that AI gets a vote in. Those teams will be built to: Engage stakeholders proactively, bringing solutions before the requisition lands Develop supplier relationships that drive innovation and performance improvement Deliver category strategies tied directly to business outcomes and enterprise objectives Earn a standing seat as a strategic partner to the business The procurement organizations that make this shift use the AI transition as the catalyst to finally become the function they were always meant to be. Procurement's AI future: lead the attack or defend the half The pitch offered a useful truth on Sunday, which is that the best teams don't win by defending. Argentina held out through 90 goalless minutes, leaned on a World Cup final record 11 saves from their keeper, and bet everything on reaching penalties. They still lost to a Spain side that kept moving the ball forward until it found a way through. Winning teams build systems where every player, goalkeeper to striker, understands the role and is set up to contribute to the attack. Procurement has spent too long pinned in its own half. Intake and orchestration AI is the substitution that finally lets the whole team move up the pitch. Every CPO faces the same choice. The transformation is coming either way; the only open question is whether they lead it or spend the next few years defending against it. The full picture, including how the builders are pulling away from the bystanders across ROI, hiring, and team design, is in our State of AI in Spend report. ‍

title: Five Retool Alternatives for Building Internal Tools: Complete Guide 2026
summary: Retool too complex for your team? Discover 5 simpler alternatives including Blitz, Appsmith, and Softr that let product managers build internal tools without a steep learning curve.
body_text: You got budget approval for an internal tool platform. The sales pitch sounded right: drag-and-drop components, quick deployment, your ops team building dashboards within days. Three weeks in, your developers are debugging JavaScript errors in the interface. Your operations lead gave up after the second tutorial. And you're explaining to leadership why the "quick win" project is now a quarter behind. Retool is the default choice for internal tool development. It's powerful, well-integrated, and backed by serious funding. But power means complexity. For PMs at growing fintech startups juggling compliance deadlines and limited engineering bandwidth , that complexity kills projects. This guide covers five alternatives that prioritize usability. Platforms that let you ship internal tools, not just demo them. What we will cover: Why product teams are looking beyond Retool What to look for in a Retool alternative 5 Retool alternatives ranked by simplicity How these alternatives compare on complexity Making the decision Getting started Why product teams are looking beyond Retool Retool is more capable than simple no-code tools but requires more technical knowledge than most teams expect. The platform assumes familiarity with JavaScript and SQL. The drag-and-drop interface handles basic layouts, but anything beyond simple forms and tables requires writing code. G2 reviews on Retool mention the learning curve 32 times, with users noting it's "somewhat complex for new users, especially those who aren't familiar with JavaScript or backend concepts." For fintech PMs, this creates a bottleneck. Your engineering team is stretched thin building core product features. Pulling them into internal tool development defeats the purpose of adopting a low-code platform. According to a study by Gartner , 70% of new enterprise applications will use low-code or no-code by 2025, up from less than 25% in 2020. Organizations adopt these platforms to reduce developer dependency. When a "low-code" tool still requires developers for most meaningful work, it fails that promise. What to look for in a Retool alternative For fintech product teams, these factors matter most: ‍ Genuine ease of use : Can someone without a dev background build functional applications? Watch for platforms that claim "no-code" but require JavaScript for basic functionality ‍ Security and compliance : SOC 2 compliance, granular access controls, audit logging. Non-negotiable for fintech! ‍ Time to first value : How long from signup to a working tool? Complex platforms require weeks of learning before productive work starts ‍ Pricing at scale : Per-seat pricing adds up fast. Know the full cost before committing ‍ Integration depth : Your tools need to connect with databases, APIs, and existing SaaS products 5 Retool alternatives ranked by simplicity Blitz Blitz was built for people who know exactly what they need to automate but don't want to wait six months for engineering to get around to it. Non-technical founders, ops leads, and PMs use it to bypass the dev bottleneck entirely. The platform bundles a database, interface builder, and workflow engine into one place. No stitching together three different tools before you can start working. Key differentiators Blitz handles complex business logic visually: Approval chains, conditional routing, multi-step workflows ; you build these by dragging and dropping, not writing JavaScript. As a result, the person who understands the process can build it directly. Security isn't an afterthought. Role-based permissions, audit trails, and data controls come standard. For fintechs and marketplaces dealing with sensitive customer data, this matters. The integrated database means you're not context-switching between a data layer and your app. Define your data model, build the interface, wire up the automation ; all in one session. Ideal for Non-technical founders at early-stage startups who can't afford to hire developers for every internal process.wor Operations leads at fintechs and marketplaces who need to build a secure KYC porta l: automate onboarding, compliance workflows, or transaction monitoring PMs at SMBs tired of waiting in the engineering backlog for tools that should take days, not quarters Pricing Blitz is currently in beta . Early access available through the website with pricing shared during onboarding. Website: blitznocode.com Blitz no code website Pros Actually no-code: complex workflows without touching JavaScript Security and permissions built in from day one Single platform for database, UI, and automation Blitz is backed by YC Cons Newer platform, smaller community Still in beta Template library growing but not as extensive as older tools Softr Most internal tools are variations of the same patterns: databases with forms, tables, and basic access control. Softr leans into this, by offering pre-built blocks you assemble into working applications. The platform connects directly to Airtable and Google Sheets. If you're already managing operations data in spreadsheets (most teams are), the barrier to entry is very low. Key differentiators Softr achieves simplicity through constraints Opinionated building blocks that cover 80% of internal tool use cases. Client portals, dashboards, inventory trackers, and simple CRMs can be assembled in hours User management and permissions work without configuration. Add team members, assign roles, restrict access, all through a visual interface. Ideal for Non-technical teams needing client portals, internal databases, or operational dashboards. Works well when existing data lives in Airtable or Google Sheets and you need a proper interface on top of it. Pricing Free plan with limited features Paid plans start at $49/month (billed annually) 3 published apps and 20 app users Website: softr.io ‍ Softr website Pros Usable by non-technical team members Direct Airtable/Google Sheets integration Fast time to first working app Strong template library Cons Limited to Airtable/Sheets/Softr database backends Less flexible for complex requirements Some components gated on higher-tier plans Appsmith Appsmith sits between Retool's complexity and pure no-code simplicity. It's open source, so your security team can audit the codebase. Drag-and-drop interface with the option to add JavaScript for complex logic. The learning curve is more gradual than Retool. Key differentiators Open source means control: Audit the codebase, Self-host without vendor lock-in. No surprises! Git-native development with GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket. Teams with established workflows get proper version control without workarounds. Ideal for Technical teams wanting low-code speed with the option to drop into code when needed. Attractive for organizations with security requirements favoring open-source or self-hosting. Pricing Free plan: $0 with unlimited users Business plan: $40/month (usage-based at $0.40/user/hour, capped at $20/user/month) 15-day free trial Website: appsmith.com Appsmith website Pros Open source, full code transparency Free self-hosting Git integration 38K+ GitHub stars, active community Enterprise security features on lower tiers than Retool Cons JavaScript knowledge needed for complex logic Client-side only Learning curve exists, though gentler than Retool UI builder occasionally buggy UI Bakery UI Bakery targets a specific pain point: enterprise features at non-enterprise prices. SSO and advanced role management at price points that make sense for growing startups. The drag-and-drop builder creates multi-step backend APIs that execute server-side: better performance than platforms running everything in the browser. Key differentiators ‍ JavaScript and Python support for backend logic. For teams with Python-heavy data pipelines, this simplifies development Workflow automation handles scheduled jobs and webhooks natively. Build a compliance report that runs every Monday, or trigger a Slack notification when transactions exceed risk thresholds. No external tools needed!
